hints.title: Forward Scanning Obstacle
hints.text: Comparing each day with every later day takes quadratic time. When a warmer day finally arrives, which earlier days does it settle, and what would you need to have kept about them?

hints.title: Monotonic Stack of Unresolved Days
hints.text: Maintain a stack of indices corresponding to temperatures in decreasing order. When a warmer temperature appears, it resolves the waiting duration for all colder days waiting at the top of the stack.

hints.title: Index Distance Resolution
hints.text: Initialize an answer array of zeros. Iterate through temperatures with index i. While the stack is not empty and current temperature exceeds the temperature at the stack top index, pop the top index and set answer[top] = i - top. Then push i onto the stack.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

complexity.notes: Monotonic decreasing stack where each index is pushed and popped at most once.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: For each day i, scanning forward for the first day j > i with T[j] > T[i] requires O(N^2) time in the worst case (e.g. monotonically non-increasing temperatures like [100, 99, 98, ...]). For N = 10^5, this requires (10^5)^2 / 2 = 5 * 10^9 inner loop comparisons, exceeding the 1-second timeout by 50x.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Storing up to O(N) unresolved day indices in a monotonic decreasing stack guarantees each index is pushed and popped at most once, reducing aggregate time from O(N^2) to amortized O(N).
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Storing indices instead of temperature values on the stack so index deltas (i - prev) can be written directly to the output array; leaving 0 for temperatures that are never exceeded.

solutions.approach: Index Distance instead of Value (Monotonic Decreasing Stack)
